parsed.summary: The Lean target says that EVERY group G : Type (with any group structure) is finitely presented and not sofic. That statement is false: the trivial group is finitely presented and satisfies the file's `Sofic` definition, and uncountable groups are not finitely presented. The paper claims that one specific group, the unit group L_{F2}(1,2)^×, is not sofic, which gives the existence of a nonsofic group. The decisive caveat is that the quantifier is ∀ where it should be ∃ (the theorem's own name says 'exists'), so the formal statement does not express the paper's result and is unprovable unless something is inconsistent.

glossary.plain: d_H(p,q) = |{y : p y ≠ q y}| / |Y| for permutations p, q of a finite set Y
glossary.note: If Y is empty, Lean's x/0 = 0 gives distance 0, but PermutationModel requires size > 0, so this case never arises.

glossary.plain: A map σ : G → Sym(n) with n > 0 and σ(1) = id; σ need not be a homomorphism.
glossary.note: Requiring σ(1) = id is a harmless normalization.

glossary.plain: σ is (F,ε)-good: d_H(σ(gh), σ(g)σ(h)) < ε for all g, h ∈ F, and d_H(σ(g), id) > 1 − ε for g ∈ F \ {1}.
For every finite F ⊆ G and every 0 < ε < 1 there is an (F,ε)-good permutation model.
glossary.note: The definition is stated for arbitrary groups, not only countable ones; it is the standard local definition.

lean_claims.plain: For every type G and every group structure on G, G is finitely presented and G is not sofic.

paper_claims.plain: The unit group of the binary Leavitt algebra L_{F2}(1,2) is not sofic; hence a nonsofic (countable) group exists.

coverage.why: Lean universally quantifies over all groups, which makes it false. Lean also adds finite presentability, which is not in the excerpt. The specific Leavitt unit group is not mentioned.

flags.explanation: The binder is `∀ (G : Type) (_ : Group G)` where `∃` was evidently intended. As written, the statement is false: the trivial group is finitely presented and sofic under the file's definition. To check soficity, take n = 1; the multiplicativity distance is 0 < ε, and separation is vacuous. The theorem therefore cannot faithfully represent any paper result.
flags.probe_idea: Prove `¬ (∀ (G : Type) (_ : Group G), Group.IsFinitelyPresented G ∧ ¬ SoficGroups.Sofic G)` by instantiating at `Unit` and building a `PermutationModel Unit` with size 1.

flags.explanation: The paper's theorem concerns the specific group L_{F2}(1,2)^×. Even an intended ∃ version would only assert existence, and it adds finite presentability. Whether L_{F2}(1,2)^× is finitely presented is not in the excerpt.
flags.probe_idea: Restate as `∃ (G : Type) (_ : Group G), Group.IsFinitelyPresented G ∧ ¬ SoficGroups.Sofic G` and check it against the paper's full text for a finite-presentation claim.
